(10 comments)
I tested the valve-monitor feature on the Ventura platform, and it works fine in our environment.
I retested this patch on the latest codebase, and it works as expected.
I don't see the inventory item in your below testing?
Tested again on the Ventura platform, and it works fine.

Overall in support of this feature, I do wonder why we're making a new application, given that going GPIO -> Dbus interface is essentially the same thing Leak detectors do, just with a few different interfaces.  was that considered?

I suspect it would be better to split these into two objects, OutputInterface and InputInterface.  Having a single object and tracking a bool to determine what mode its in seems like more trouble than it's worth in terms of interfaces (evidence by now needing to add if(!inputMode) below.)
As written, don't all of these need inputMode checks?  See comment above about splitting up things.
You have two interfaces that inherit from associations?
Why are these two separate with multiple inheritance?  SHouldn't they both be in the same object?
this seems like we should specify the type of state, why aren't we?

1. We generally don't use bools
2. We probably want to define this as "asserted" in some fashion.  Maybe the same way we do inverted GPIOs elsewhere?  As written this isn't very clear what it does.

Is there a more specific type we can use here?  The valves I know of are Assert open, deassert close.  Obviously this one is more complicated, so lets give it a name.  I'm not sure what that would be though.  If you have an example datasheet for one of these values, I can help suggest more things.
sensors/valve_open isn't a namespace, and this isn't a sensor under the normal definitions.  What that path discussed somewhere?
